acceptanceCriteria: A newer valid supersede receipt deterministically resolves older successor-binding residue for archived predecessors without rewriting historical bytes.
Malformed, foreign, tampered, missing, or newer invalid recovery records remain fail-closed and are never silently ignored.
WI-424 and WI-426 historical recovery chains can be rendered and closed through the supported Runtime lifecycle, and ordinary Work Item entry remains blocked when no valid supersede exists.
Regression tests cover valid supersede after invalid successor binding, no-valid-supersede fail-closed behavior, and immutable predecessor bytes.
Three-language workflow/parity documentation states the historical projection boundary and evidence-preservation rule.
goal: Prevent historical recovery residue from blocking valid predecessor closure or the next Work Item while preserving fail-closed behavior for malformed or untrusted records.
intent: Make archived recovery history deterministic when older successor-binding attempts coexist with a newer valid supersede, without rewriting immutable evidence.
outOfScope: Broad recovery graph redesign or Runtime architecture split
